findings.title: Approval spender does not match execution venue — every ERC20-input swap on the 'tegridy' or 'uniswap' route cannot execute
findings.evidence: useSwapAllowance.ts:113 picks the spender as `const spender = selectedRoute === 'tegridy' ? TEGRIDY_ROUTER_ADDRESS : SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS;` (and the allowance reads at lines 52-78 check those same two spenders). But useSwap.ts executes the 'tegridy' route through SwapFeeRouter (line 423-427: `address: SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS ... functionName: 'swapExactTokensForETH'`) and the 'uniswap' route through the real Uniswap router (line 473-477: `address: UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER ... swapExactTokensForETH`). SwapFeeRouter.sol:747 does `IERC20(path[0]).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amountIn)` — it needs allowance to SFR, not TegridyRouter; Uniswap Router02 likewise pulls from msg.sender and needs allowance to itself, not SFR. Git confirms the regression: 43c3ddb ('route genuine-Uniswap trades to the real Uniswap router') and 003445e ('capture the 0.5% protocol fee on native-pool routes') both postdate the last commit touching useSwapAllowance.ts (4b3a47f). Net effect today (TOWELI sell = ERC20-input, native pool empty, route='uniswap'): user approves SFR, swap goes to UniswapV2Router, transferFrom fails — wallet gas-estimation error or on-chain revert. After LP seed (route='tegridy'): user approves TegridyRouter, swap goes to SFR, same failure. The only working ERC20-input path is aggregator-route-with-tegridy-fallback (approves SFR, executes SFR). ETH-input swaps are unaffected (no approval).
findings.suggestion: Make the spender map 1:1 to the executor: 'tegridy' → SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS, 'uniswap' → UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER, aggregator → whichever on-chain fallback (selectedOnChainRoute.source) executes. Add a unit test asserting spender === writeContract target per route.

findings.title: DCA and browser limit-orders quote Uniswap prices but execute via SwapFeeRouter→TegridyRouter (the thin/empty native pool) — guaranteed reverts or mispriced minOut
findings.evidence: useDCA.ts:434-439 fetches minOut from `address: UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER ... getAmountsOut`, then lines 497-529 execute on `address: SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS` (whose inner router is TegridyRouter — the same wiring documented in useSwap.ts:397-400 'SFR is wired to the native TegridyRouter... a Uniswap-priced minOut sent through it executes on the (currently thin) native pool and reverts'). useLimitOrders.ts has the identical pattern: price-poll + re-quote on UNISWAP_V2_ROUTER (lines 320-330, 481-492) but executeOrder writes to SWAP_FEE_ROUTER_ADDRESS (lines 402-435). The deep-pool routing fix that was applied to useSwap (commit 43c3ddb) was never propagated to these two keepers. With the native TOWELI/WETH pool unseeded, every triggered DCA tick / limit fill reverts (or the native pair's getAmountsOut revert makes minOut games moot); after seeding, the Uniswap-priced floor frequently exceeds what the native pool can deliver.
findings.suggestion: Either quote and execute on the same venue (quote SFR's own router path), or route DCA/limit executions to the venue that produced the quote (UniswapV2Router) like useSwap now does — keeping the allowance check pointed at the same contract.

findings.title: Swap success effect re-fires every render for ~4s — duplicate 'WAGMI! Swap confirmed' toasts, phantom swap-confirmed toast after a plain approve, duplicated trackSwap analytics
findings.evidence: useSwap.ts:246-286: the receipt-success effect's dep array includes `allowance` (the object returned by useSwapAllowance is a fresh literal every render — not memoized, useSwapAllowance.ts:195-204) and `inputAmount`/`quote.selectedRoute`. While isSuccess is latched true (until the 4s `reset()` at line 284), useSwapQuote's 1-second staleness ticker (useSwapQuote.ts:261-265 `setInterval(() => setNow(Date.now()), 1000)`) re-renders the consumer every second, so the effect re-runs each tick. On re-run after an approve, `lastActionRef.current` was already nulled by the first run (line 263), so control falls through to the swap branch: `toast.success('WAGMI! Swap confirmed'...)` (line 268, no toast id → sonner stacks duplicates) and `trackSwap(...)` (line 278) fire again with fallback live values. Result: stacked duplicate success toasts after a swap, a phantom 'Swap confirmed' toast ~1s after a mere token approval, and inflated swap analytics.
findings.suggestion: Guard with a lastHandledHashRef (the pattern already used in useLPFarming.ts:80-95), give the toast `id: hash`, and remove unstable deps (memoize the useSwapAllowance return object).

findings.title: normalizeTokenAddress 'zero' style returns the 0xEeee sentinel instead of the zero address — Odos native-ETH quotes silently dead
findings.evidence: aggregator.ts:35-39: `case 'zero': return '0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE';` — identical to the 'native' case. getOdosQuote (lines 116-117) calls `normalizeTokenAddress(tokenIn, 'zero')` because Odos expects 0x0000...0000 for native ETH; sending the 0xEeee address makes Odos reject the quote (res.ok false → null, swallowed by the catch). The meta-aggregator silently loses Odos as a source for every ETH-input swap — exactly the headline ETH→TOWELI flow.
findings.suggestion: Return '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' from the 'zero' branch and add a test for the Odos native-input path.

findings.title: refreshQuote never re-fetches aggregator quotes — after the 30s staleness gate trips, the aggregator leg is permanently lost until the user edits the input
findings.evidence: useSwapQuote.ts:437-446: `refreshQuote` bumps `quoteRequestIdRef.current += 1` with the comment 'bumping the requestId triggers re-fetch', but the aggregator fetch effect's deps are `[fromToken, toToken, parsedAmount, address, fromDecimals, chainId]` (line 251) — none change, so the effect never re-runs. `setAggQuoteResult(null)` just deletes the existing aggregator quote. So when useSwap.ts:343-347 blocks a stale swap and calls refreshQuote, only the on-chain legs refetch; the 7-aggregator comparison silently downgrades to on-chain-only, and the user can submit a worse route without knowing. Also, if the refetched uniAmountsOut is structurally identical, the quoteFetchedAt stamp effect (lines 254-258) never re-fires, leaving quoteFetchedAt=0 which makes isQuoteStale read false with no fresh stamp.
findings.suggestion: Drive the aggregator effect from a state-based requestId (useState counter included in the dep array) so refreshQuote actually re-fires it, and stamp quoteFetchedAt from the refetch promises.

findings.title: POOL_LAUNCH_TIMESTAMP hardcoded to 2025-03-01 — ~15 months before the pool existed — understating fee-based APR and '24h volume' by ~100x once fees accrue
findings.evidence: usePoolTVL.ts:10 `const POOL_LAUNCH_TIMESTAMP = new Date('2025-03-01').getTime() / 1000;` — but TEGRIDY_LP_ADDRESS was deployed in the 2026-06-06 relaunch (constants.ts:15-18). Lines 76-82 divide cumulative totalETHFees by poolAgeDays computed from that date (~466 days instead of ~5), so `dailyFees`, `aprNum`, and `vol24h` are ~100x too low the moment real fees exist. Additionally the displayed 'vol24h' is a lifetime daily average mislabeled as 24h.
findings.suggestion: Set the constant to the actual pair-creation timestamp (or read the pair's first-mint block once and cache), and label the figure 'avg daily volume'.

findings.title: eth_getLogs scans start at stale fromBlock 18000000 (Sep 2023) against contracts deployed June 2026 — public RPCs reject the wide range, silently zeroing swap count and loyalty score
findings.evidence: usePoints.ts:73-83 (`fromBlock: 18000000n` for SwapExecuted on the relaunch SwapFeeRouter) and useTegridyScore.ts:322-343 (same fromBlock for Staked on the relaunch staking contract). Both catch handlers silently fall back to 0 (`.catch(() => { ... setSwapCount(0) })`, and the score hook's own comment admits 'Public RPCs sometimes reject wide eth_getLogs ranges'). The configured transports (publicnode/ankr/llamarpc, wagmi.ts:12-21) all cap getLogs ranges well below the ~5M-block span requested, so points/activity/loyalty scores quietly read 0 for most users.
findings.suggestion: Hardcode the actual relaunch deploy block (a constant next to the addresses in constants.ts) as fromBlock, or chunk the scan.

findings.title: IPFS gateway list leads with cloudflare-ipfs.com (gateway sunset by Cloudflare in 2024) and resolveSafeUrl/safeUrl return ONLY that first gateway for consumers — ipfs:// images render broken with no fallback
findings.evidence: imageSafety.ts:57-61 `IPFS_GATEWAYS = ['https://cloudflare-ipfs.com/ipfs/', 'https://dweb.link/ipfs/', 'https://ipfs.io/ipfs/']` and resolveSafeUrl (lines 80-83) returns `IPFS_GATEWAYS[0]` for any ipfs:// URI. fetchWithIpfsFallback does race the list, but the `` consumers (safeUrl → CollectionDetailV2.tsx:12, useNFTDropV2 resolveAssetUrl) get a single dead-host URL. Cloudflare publicly deprecated/shut its public IPFS gateway in 2024 (external infra fact — verify with one fetch; if it 410s, every ipfs-hosted collection image is currently broken).
findings.suggestion: Reorder so a live gateway is first (ipfs.io or dweb.link), or better: have ArtImg/NftImage onError advance through ipfsCandidates().

findings.title: The 60s 'refetch' interval is a no-op — `setTokenLoading((p) => p)` sets identical state, so open-loan data and overdue status never refresh
findings.evidence: useMyLoans.ts:117-121: `const id = setInterval(() => { ... setTokenLoading((p) => p); }, REFETCH_MS);` with comment 'Re-trigger by toggling state'. Setting state to the same value bails out of re-render in React, and even a re-render would not re-run the fetch effect because its deps `[publicClient, onMainnet, tokenDeployed, tokenCount, address]` are unchanged. The NFT-loans effect (lines 125-163) has no interval at all, and `status: 'overdue'` is computed from a `now` captured once in useMemo (line 167) whose deps exclude time. Inert today (both lending addresses zeroed) but it is the recovery-pass code that will ship when lending un-gates.
findings.suggestion: Use a state tick (`setTick(t => t+1)`) included in the effect deps, or move the sweep into tanstack-query with refetchInterval.

findings.title: useTrackedTransactionReceipt reads fields wagmi never returns (receiptStatus/blockNumber/errorName at top level) — a reverted tx would report status 'confirmed'; currently dead code
findings.evidence: useTransactionReceipt.ts:117-127 casts the wagmi result to `{ receiptStatus?: 'success' | 'reverted'; blockNumber?: bigint; errorName?: string }`, but wagmi v2 exposes these as `data.status`, `data.blockNumber`, and `error.name`. Only the test mock (src/test-utils/wagmi-mocks.ts:185 'Additive passthrough for useTrackedTransactionReceipt') supplies the flat fields, so the tests pass while the runtime branch `result.receiptStatus === 'reverted'` (line 155) can never trip — a reverted receipt falls through to `status: 'confirmed'` (line 164). Grep shows no app component consumes the hook (only tests/mocks), so the R044 H3 'reorg defense' is both unwired and incorrect at runtime.
findings.suggestion: Read `data?.status` / `error?.name` from the real hook result, then actually adopt it in the tx-toast hooks (or delete it).

findings.title: All three R080 zod schema files are dead code — never imported by the boundaries they document
findings.evidence: Grep for `schemas/(aggregator|geckoTerminal|opensea)` across src returns zero matches. lib/aggregator.ts still validates by hand (e.g. line 94 `typeof data.amountOut !== 'string' || !/^\d+$/.test(...)`), useToweliPrice.ts:121 walks `d?.data?.attributes?.token_prices` untyped, and nakamigos api consumers use raw .json(). Each schema file even carries instructions ('Apply via parseOrNull(schema, data) at every such boundary') that were never executed, and parseOrNull is duplicated 3x.
findings.suggestion: Wire parseOrNull into the seven aggregator parsers, the two GeckoTerminal call sites, and the OpenSea proxy consumers — or delete the files so future audits don't assume the validation exists.

findings.title: The purpose-built txErrors helper is unused in the money paths — wallet cancellations render as scary red 'Transaction failed' / raw error toasts in 8+ hooks
findings.evidence: Grep: surfaceTxError/isUserRejection are imported only by GaugeVoting.tsx (plus the unrelated mevProtection copy). Meanwhile useFarmActions.ts:76, useLPFarming.ts:111, useAddLiquidity.ts:159, useRestaking.ts:142 all toast `writeError.message?.slice(0, 120)` raw; useRevenueStats.ts:100 and useBribes.ts:345 toast generic 'Transaction failed' for any writeError including user rejection; useNFTDropV2.ts:232 toasts 'Mint failed' on rejection. txErrors.ts exists precisely to classify UserRejectedRequestError (including the nested-cause walk, lines 56-72) as a soft 'Cancelled' info toast.
findings.suggestion: Replace the per-hook raw toasts with surfaceTxError(err, toast, { component }) — one mechanical sweep.

findings.title: Module-level sessionStorage/crypto.randomUUID access can crash the whole app at import time in storage-blocked or non-secure contexts; failed-flush queue is unbounded
findings.evidence: analytics.ts:20-30: `getSessionId()` runs at module scope (`const sessionId = getSessionId();`) with no try/catch — browsers with storage disabled (cookie-blocked iframes/webviews) throw SecurityError from `sessionStorage.getItem`, and `crypto.randomUUID()` requires a secure context — either kills the bundle at import. Also lines 72-83: on fetch failure the batch is re-queued forever (`queue = [...batch, ...queue]`) with no cap, so a down endpoint grows memory for the life of the tab.
findings.suggestion: Wrap getSessionId in try/catch with a Math.random fallback, and cap the queue (e.g. drop oldest past 200 events).

findings.title: Stale contradictory comment block above LP_FARMING_ADDRESS still says the address is ZEROED and must be restored
findings.evidence: constants.ts:25-27 reads '// ZEROED 2026-05-31 (relaunch supersedes Wave 0...)... Restore the real address after the relaunch redeploy.' directly above line 28 which now holds the live relaunch address 0x1171268A... (deployed 2026-06-08). Anyone skimming the gating table will misread the farm as gated.
findings.suggestion: Delete the stale ZEROED comment; keep only the RELAUNCH note.

findings.title: Refund transactions toast 'Mint confirmed!' / 'Mint failed'
findings.evidence: useNFTDropV2.ts:225-236: the single receipt effect toasts `toast.success('Mint confirmed!')` and `toast.error('Mint failed')` for any hash, but the hook also submits `refund()` (line 204) through the same writeContract — a successful refund shows 'Mint confirmed!'.
findings.suggestion: Track lastAction ('mint'|'refund') in a ref, mirror useSwap's lastActionRef pattern.

findings.title: categorizeTx matches zeroed-contract addresses — any tx to 0x000...0 (ETH burns) is labeled 'Restake'
findings.evidence: txHistory.ts:97 `if (to === TEGRIDY_RESTAKING_ADDRESS.toLowerCase())` — TEGRIDY_RESTAKING_ADDRESS is the zero address (constants.ts:7), as are COMMUNITY_GRANTS/MEME_BOUNTY/PREMIUM/VOTE_INCENTIVES below it, so the first zero-compare wins and a burn/zero-send row gets categorized 'Restake'.
findings.suggestion: Skip comparisons for addresses failing isDeployed().

findings.title: Default token list ships legacy MATIC (Polygon migrated to POL in Sept 2024)
findings.evidence: tokenList.ts:106-111: `symbol: 'MATIC', name: 'Polygon', address: 0x7D1AfA7B...` — the legacy token; best-in-class lists show POL (0x455e53...). Cosmetic but signals staleness in a curated list.
findings.suggestion: Add POL (keep MATIC if you want the legacy pair tradable).

findings.title: Score tip and streak copy reference the removed daily-visit streak mechanic
findings.evidence: useTegridyScore.ts:155 tip says 'Visit daily and swap to build your streak', but pointsEngine.ts:194-197 deprecated recordDailyVisit to a no-op ('Daily visit streaks removed -- not verifiable on-chain'), so the streak can never grow and the tip is unactionable.
findings.suggestion: Reword the activity tip to swaps/staking only.

findings.title: R042 HIGH-2 return-object memoization is defeated — `path` is a new array every render, so the memo (and routeDescription) recompute every render anyway
findings.evidence: useSwapQuote.ts:75 `const path = fromToken && toToken ? buildPath(fromToken, toToken) : [];` creates a fresh array each render; it is in the final useMemo dep list (line 496) whose stated purpose is 'consumers don't see a fresh identity on every render' (lines 463-465). Identity therefore flips every render regardless.
findings.suggestion: useMemo the path on [fromToken, toToken].

findings.title: flush() drops the batch on HTTP error responses — only network failures persist to localStorage
findings.evidence: errorReporting.ts:137-147: `fetch(endpoint, {...}).catch(() => persistToLocalStorage(toSend))` — fetch only rejects on network errors; a 4xx/5xx resolves, res.ok is never checked, and the batch is silently lost.
findings.suggestion: Add `.then(r => { if (!r.ok) persistToLocalStorage(toSend); })`.

findings.title: Polling load and inconsistency: limit orders fire up to 50 sequential getAmountsOut every 15s; CoW poll lacks the hidden-tab gate the other keepers have
findings.evidence: useLimitOrders.ts:41 PRICE_POLL_INTERVAL=15_000 with a per-active-order readContract loop (lines 473-503, MAX_ORDERS=50) — heaviest poller in the app on public RPCs. useCowLimitOrder.ts:259-264 polls every 30s without the `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'` skip that useDCA.ts:556 and useLimitOrders.ts:511 both apply.
findings.suggestion: Batch the order quotes in a single multicall per tick and add the visibility gate to the CoW poll.

findings.title: Minor inconsistencies: un-cleaned setTimeout(reset) timers, and stake() throws while sibling actions return silently
findings.evidence: useAddLiquidity.ts:146/153/160 schedule `setTimeout(() => reset(), 4000)` inside effects without cleanup (harmless but leaky vs the cleanup pattern used in useSwap.ts:284-285). useFarmActions.ts:99 `if (wei === null) throw new Error('Invalid amount');` — an exception in an onClick path, while approve() at line 85 silently returns for the same condition.
findings.suggestion: Return + toast instead of throw; clear the timers in effect cleanup.

findings.title: Fabricated '(est.)' volume/APR from an assumed turnover ratio contradicts the project's honesty-pass standard
findings.evidence: usePoolTVL.ts:93-103: when no fees exist, vol24h is invented as `tvl * dailyVolumeRatio` with ratios 0.01-0.04 picked by TVL bucket, and APR derived from that fiction. It is labeled '~ (est.)' but renders a number the chain can't back — the exact pattern constants.ts:116-122 forbids for the season banner ('nothing should render a number the chain can't back').
findings.suggestion: Show '—' with a 'volume appears after first trades' microcopy instead of synthetic estimates (additive copy change, no section removal).

findings.title: Negative-value formatting quirks and 88 raw .toFixed() call sites bypassing the central util
findings.evidence: formatting.ts:11 renders negatives as `$-12.34` (sign inside, vs convention `-$12.34`) and formatNumber gives `-5000.00` without thousands separators (line 20 falls through all >= checks for negatives). Grep counts 88 `.toFixed(` occurrences across 24 component files despite formatCurrency/formatNumber/formatTokenAmount existing — number formatting is scattered, not centralized.
findings.suggestion: Handle sign in formatCurrency/formatNumber and sweep components onto the utils.

findings.title: Dead exports worth pruning or wiring: ERROR_COPY, randomToweliQuote, poolFlavorLabel, lockLabelForSeconds, useTrackedTransactionReceipt, the EIP-5792 foundation
findings.evidence: Grep shows ERROR_COPY, randomToweliQuote, poolFlavorLabel and lockLabelForSeconds are defined in copy.ts (lines 121-152) with no consumers; useTrackedTransactionReceipt is consumed only by tests/mocks; eip5792.ts is self-described 'FOUNDATION ONLY (2026-06-01)' and still unwired into approve+swap/stake despite being a Tier-1 roadmap item.
findings.suggestion: Either wire them (ERROR_COPY into the txErrors sweep, EIP-5792 into the approve+swap path) or delete to keep the audit surface honest.

findings.title: Price alerts are device-global but the cap message says 'per wallet'; sendNotification fires inside a state updater (double-fires under StrictMode); unused _currentPrice param
findings.evidence: usePriceAlerts.ts:15 single STORAGE_KEY 'tegridy-price-alerts' (no address scoping) while line 107 toasts 'Up to 20 price alerts per wallet'; lines 69-88 call sendNotification inside the setAlerts updater — updaters can run twice in dev StrictMode. usePriceHistory.ts:25 takes `_currentPrice?: number` that is never used.
findings.suggestion: Move the notification out of the updater, fix the copy, drop the dead param.

findings.title: rpc.ankr.com/eth in the fallback list likely requires an API key now (unverified) — would make slot 2 a guaranteed-miss before rank() heals it
findings.evidence: wagmi.ts:15 `http('https://rpc.ankr.com/eth')` — Ankr moved its public endpoints behind registration/keyed access (external infra change; unverified hypothesis — confirm with one curl). The llamarpc comment (lines 16-17) shows the team already tracks dead public RPCs; ankr may be in the same state. rank:true mitigates but first-hit users still pay the timeout.
findings.suggestion: Curl-test the three public RPCs in CI weekly, or swap ankr for drpc/1rpc.

findings.title: POLAccumulator marked live:false on Tokenomics despite being deployed in the 2026-06-06 relaunch
findings.evidence: TokenomicsPage.tsx:44 `{ label: 'POLAccumulator', address: POL_ACCUMULATOR_ADDRESS, live: false }` while constants.ts:23 holds the live relaunch address 0x2A5f65f4... (RELAUNCH 2026-06-06 comment). Found while verifying address-table consistency; the page file itself was outside this audit's assigned scope, so flagging for the page-auditor to confirm rendering impact.
findings.suggestion: Derive `live` from isDeployed(address) instead of a hand-maintained flag.
